units.source_en: But this conclusion is highly dependent on the size of the extra dimensions.
The reason is that in stringlM-theory, the strength of the gravitational force we observe in our three extended dimensions repre sents an interplay between two factors.

paragraphs.source_en: One factor is the intrinsic, fundamental strength of the gravitational force. The second factor is the size of the extra dimensions. The larger the extra dimensions, the more gravity can spill into them and the weaker its force will appear in the familiar dimensions. Just as larger pipes yield weaker water pressure because they allow water more room to spread out, so larger extra dimensions yield weaker gravity, because they give gravity more room to spread out.
